short: Visionary civil engineer who transformed 19th-century transport with unprecedented projects.
full:
Isambard Kingdom Brunel was the defining engineering genius of the Victorian age, known for his relentless ambition and willingness to push technology to its absolute limits. As chief engineer of the Great Western Railway, he designed a revolutionary broad-gauge network of viaducts, tunnels, and stations that connected London to the West Country with unprecedented speed and smoothness.

Beyond railways, Brunel revolutionised maritime transport by designing a series of increasingly massive steamships. The SS Great Western inaugurated regular transatlantic steam travel, while the iron-hulled SS Great Britain pioneered the screw propeller. His final project, the gargantuan SS Great Eastern, was the largest ship built in the 19th century and successfully laid the first transatlantic telegraph cable.
